habitat: Singly or in pairs on secluded ponds with dense fringing vegetation. It climbs tangled reeds, walks on water lilies or swims.
summary: An uncommon and irregular late-summer resident. A small, large-footed waterbird with green upper parts, a dark blue body, neck and head, and a red bill and red legs. The frontal shield varies from dull apple-green to blueish, and is not all red like African Swamphen. The identification line also says the shield is blue. The immature is not described in the text. The call is a series of clicks, dik-dik-dik-dik, or a rolling purrrrr-pur-pur-pur in courtship. Newman does not name the months, so they are unset. The Kemp name Lesser Gallinule and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Swamphen is larger, with an entirely red frontal shield and bill and pink legs. Allen’s Gallinule has a shield that varies from dull apple-green to blueish.

calls.description: Rapid clicks, dik-dik-dik-dik, or a melodious rolling purrrrr-pur-pur-pur in courtship. The grade A recordings are ND. Grade B call from Ankarafantsika National Park, Madagascar. The licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The filename is XC162127-Allen's GallinuleAK12013.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon and irregular late-summer resident and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The shield colour varies, so it is not stored as one colour. The immature is only said to be as illustrated. The grade A recordings are ND, so the playable file is grade B from Madagascar. The Kemp name Lesser Gallinule and the code NB were left unchanged.
